the two-timescale learning algorithm proposed in the paper can be viewed as a decentralized variant of the Q-learning dynamics in zero-sum Markov game, and the algorithm is guaranteed to converge to the best response when the opponents follow a stationary policy, and to the Nash equilibrium when both agents adopt it.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the convergence of a decentralized MARL algorithm in zero-sum games does not require any coordination among agents, nor any prior knowledge about the opponent or game.

, in a radically uncoupling setting, the agents need to be aware of their own payoffs but not of the opponent's payoffs, and need to update their policies at a slow timescale to achieve convergence to the equilibrium.

the two-timescale learning framework, a standard approach to address non-stationarity in reinforcement learning, is also effective in the decentralized MARL setting, where the non-stationary environment is caused by the simultaneous adaptation of multiple agents rather than the stochasticity of the environment.
